The role

Gauntlet is looking for an AI Research Engineer to help improve how we build, evaluate and use AI agents across the business.

We already have agents running in production, including Aria, our in-house generalist agent. They're used across research, engineering and business workflows, and we've learned a lot from seeing how they perform in practice. Some tasks work extremely well; others produce inconsistent results, and changes to models or tooling can introduce unexpected problems. Today, much of that feedback is still subjective. We want to build a more systematic way of understanding what works, what doesn't and why.

A major part of this role will be building the evaluation frameworks that allow us to measure agent performance on real tasks. You'll work with our engineers, quantitative researchers and other teams to understand where agents struggle, turn those observations into measurable experiments, and use the results to improve the systems we're building.

You'll also contribute directly to our existing agents and internal tooling. Initially, the work will be more engineering-focused as you get familiar with our systems, shipping improvements and integrations that teams can use. Over time, you'll take on more open-ended research, helping us develop better approaches to evaluation, agent behaviour and infrastructure.

We're also thinking beyond individual agents. One of our longer-term goals is to build a shared system of knowledge and reusable skills that our agents can draw from and improve over time. You'll play an important role in developing that infrastructure and how we evaluate its effectiveness.

This is an applied research role with a meaningful engineering component. We're looking for someone who enjoys investigating difficult problems, can design good experiments and is comfortable building and shipping the solutions that come out of them.

Gauntlet builds the financial systems of the future. While much of onchain finance is focused on point solutions, we operate across the entire stack to offer best-in-class vault products. Today we serve over $1.7B in client TVL across some of the largest fintechs/neobanks, protocols, exchanges, and capital allocators in crypto - and, increasingly, traditional asset management. Our team brings together traditional finance and crypto-native expertise to deliver durable, sophisticated products for institutional clients moving onchain.

  • Experience building tools or systems that other people use, with an understanding of how to evaluate their effectiveness beyond technical benchmarks.
  • Comfort working across research and engineering, collaborating with different teams and adapting as priorities change.
  • Genuine interest in AI agents and how they can be made more capable, reliable and useful.

  • Familiarity with AI security considerations, including access controls, prompt injection and data protection.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.
 

About the Team

OKX Internal Audit is the organization's independent third line of defense, reporting to the Board and the Group Audit and Risk Committee on the design and effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal controls across a global, multi-entity crypto exchange. The function executes a risk-based annual audit plan covering financial, operational, technology, security, and regulatory risk, and operates with full, unrestricted access to systems, records, and personnel.
Within Internal Audit, the Platform & Infrastructure team sits inside the Global Platform & Engineering (GP&E) team and owns assurance over the technology foundation that keeps the exchange running: network administration, cloud infrastructure and infrastructure-as-code, containerization and orchestration, middleware services, site reliability and disaster recovery, and the data pipelines feeding OKX's financial and operational systems. Reflecting a multi-cloud environment (AWS, Alibaba Cloud, GCP) supporting live trading, custody, and customer-facing operations on a global scale.
 

About the Role

As Senior Manager, Platform & Infrastructure Audit, you'll be a hands-on, deeply technical individual-contributor auditor who owns critical assurance projects spanning the cloud infrastructure and DevOps lifecycle, from platform build and configuration through CI/CD pipelines and hands-on ITGC validation. You'll bring subject matter expertise to both dimensions of AI in scope: auditing AI (assessing how OKX's AI/ML systems are built, governed, and monitored) and auditing with AI (applying AI tools to your own scoping, testing, and reporting) while also flexing into adjacent domains such as cloud security and identity, resilience engineering, secure SDLC, and data engineering. You'll help shape the risk-based audit plan by identifying emerging infrastructure risks, and partner closely with Engineering, SRE, and Security stakeholders to deliver findings and recommendations that hold up in a fast-moving, high-technology crypto environment.
 

What You'll be Doing 

  • Cloud Infrastructure & Platform Engineering Audit (SME): Deep, hands-on expertise auditing cloud platforms (Alibaba Cloud, AWS), containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm).
  • AI Use, Adoption & Governance: Two dimensions, both required.
    • Auditing AI: Assessing how AI/ML systems are built, deployed, and monitored — model and data lineage, training-data provenance and quality, access to models and prompts, human-in-the-loop and approval controls, evaluation and drift monitoring, and alignment to emerging AI governance and regulatory expectations.
    • Auditing with AI: A demonstrated bias toward using AI in your own audit work — scoping, evidence review, control testing, script generation, and reporting — and an interest in helping the function build reusable AI-enabled audit tooling.

What We Look For in You

  • Crypto & Blockchain Acumen: Prior experience at a crypto exchange or with a crypto product is preferred.
  • Critical Thinking for Complex Environments: A proven capacity to analyze novel technical and control environments unique to crypto, identify intricate root causes, and propose effective, context-specific remediation that engineering teams will actually adopt.
  • Breadth Across Adjacent Platform Domains: Demonstrable experience auditing control design and operating effectiveness in several of the following:
    • Cloud security and identity — IAM, network segmentation, secrets management, encryption and key management
    • Site reliability and resilience — observability, incident and problem management, capacity, backup and disaster recovery
    • Software development lifecycle — code review, branch protection, artifact integrity, secure SDLC, third-party and open-source dependency risk
    • Data engineering and analytics — integrity and quality of data pipelines and ETL processes
    • AI/ML platform and MLOps — model registries, feature stores, inference infrastructure, and the data feeding them

Nice to Haves

  • Cloud or Security Certifications: AWS or GCP professional-level certification, Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), CISA, CISSP, or CCSK/CCSP.
  • Crypto and blockchain literacy: regulated financial-services, fintech, or crypto experience.
  • Mandarin speaking

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Renewals Team partners with account teams to deliver successful contract renewals, protect margins, and grow Stripe’s existing revenue base. We bring commercial expertise to renewal planning and execution, including understanding historical consumption and pricing, positioning customer value, identifying risk, and surfacing upsell and cross-sell opportunities. Our focus is on building a proactive, consistent renewal motion that delivers strong outcomes for Stripe and our users.

What you’ll do

As the head of EMEA & APAC Renewals, you will lead a distributed team of Renewals Specialists and build regional refinement on a globally consistent model, including driving a proactive renewal motion across the two regions. You will partner with global and regional Sales leaders, Customer Success, Sales Strategy & Operations, and other internal partners to translate global priorities into regional plans, strengthen account-team engagement, and scale how we support renewals across markets and customer segments.

We are looking for a commercial leader who combines strong renewal and negotiation judgment with the ability to build high-performing teams and durable operating processes. You will bring clarity in an ambiguous, high-growth environment, turn commercial insights into action, and build trusted partnerships with field leaders at every level.

Responsibilities

  • Set and execute the EMEA and APAC renewals strategy, translating global priorities into regional and segment-specific plans that improve retention, support expansion, and protect sustainable commercial outcomes.
  • Build a proactive renewal motion with Sales and Customer Success, establishing early account planning, clear responsibilities, and consistent specialist partnerships. Enable engagement 12–18 months ahead of renewal where appropriate to the customer segment and deal complexity.
  • Build trusted partnerships across account executives and front-line, second-line, and regional sales leaders, ensuring renewal insights inform account and territory plans and translate into clear action.
  • Establish a rigorous regional operating cadence for renewal forecasting, risk inspection, deal strategy, and escalation. Turn portfolio insights into actionable recommendations for field leaders and track follow-through.
  • Design team coverage and capacity plans that balance strategic deal support with scalable engagement across the renewal portfolio.
  • Recruit, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Renewals Specialists, strengthening negotiation skills, commercial judgment, and strategic account-team partnership while supporting individual career growth.
  • Provide strategic guidance on complex renewals and serve as an executive sponsor or senior escalation partner for key customer relationships.
  • Scale shared playbooks, systems, and AI-enabled workflows, with clear quality standards, human review, and accountability for adoption and delivery. Maintain a consistent global baseline while adapting execution to regional and segment needs.
  • Surface recurring customer and commercial insights to inform improvements to renewal playbooks, tooling, and cross-functional execution.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in renewals, customer success, account management, or technology sales, including 5+ years of people leadership, with a demonstrated track record of delivering retention and growth outcomes for existing customers.
  • Experience leading geographically distributed commercial teams across multiple markets and cultures, with the ability to adapt engagement models to regional and customer-segment needs.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex renewal or existing-customer negotiations, balancing customer value, retention, expansion, pricing, and sustainable commercial outcomes.
  • Proven ability to build trusted partnerships with senior Sales and Customer Success leaders, align teams around shared priorities, and establish clear responsibilities in a matrixed organization.
  • Experience building proactive renewal engagement models that bring account teams together early to identify risks, establish account strategies, and uncover expansion opportunities.
  • Strong analytical and operational judgment, including renewal forecasting, performance inspection, and translating customer consumption, pricing, and commercial data into clear recommendations and action.
  • Experience designing and scaling team coverage, capacity plans, and repeatable operating processes in a high-growth technology environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing teams, strengthening both commercial judgment and strategic account-team partnership.
  • Ability to translate long-term strategy into clear priorities, delivery commitments, and measurable execution, while operating effectively through ambiguity.
  • Strong executive communication skills, with the ability to advise senior stakeholders and engage directly in strategic customer negotiations and escalations.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience leading a dedicated renewals organization.
  • Experience working across both EMEA and APAC.
  • Familiarity with payments, financial infrastructure, or consumption-based commercial models.
  • Experience applying automation and AI to improve commercial workflows, with clear standards for adoption, quality, and human review.

About the role

We are seeking an Inference Performance Engineer to make Bitdeer AI's MaaS platform's benchmarks, capacity plans, and cost projections trustworthy proxies for what customers actually run in production. Today, load tests are built on prompt and output length assumptions and concurrency patterns that were reasonable a quarter ago but no longer match the traffic mix flowing through chat, completion, and embedding endpoints — the result is GPU fleets sized against a workload that doesn't exist, cost-per-token figures that surprise finance at quarter close, and latency percentile dashboards that different teams calculate differently and therefore don't trust. This role exists to close that gap: characterizing real production traffic shapes, keeping benchmarking harnesses honest against that reality, and turning the results into capacity and unit-economics numbers the business can plan around with confidence. The person who thrives here is a rigorous, data-first systems thinker who is equally comfortable pulling apart a token-length histogram, arguing with a serving-stack engineer about tail latency, and explaining a GPU-hour cost model to finance — someone who treats every metric definition as a contract other teams will build on, not a throwaway number.

What you will be responsible for:

  • Traffic and Workload Characterization: Continuously profile real production request streams across chat, completions, embeddings, and fine-tuning endpoints to build and maintain statistical models of prompt length, output length, concurrency, and burstiness by model and customer segment. Surface how these distributions shift over time and by tenant so that benchmarking, capacity, and pricing decisions are grounded in what the platform actually serves rather than stale assumptions. Package these findings into reusable traffic profiles other teams can pull from directly.
  • Harness-to-Production Fidelity: Own the validation loop between internal load-testing and benchmarking harnesses and live production behavior, auditing synthetic workload generators against the traffic profiles you maintain and flagging drift before it corrupts a capacity or optimization decision. Work with the inference serving team to update harness configurations, request mixes, and concurrency patterns whenever production shifts. Treat every benchmark result as suspect until it has been reconciled against real telemetry.
  • Capacity Planning and Unit Economics: Translate workload characterization and GPU utilization data into capacity forecasts and cost-per-token or cost-per-request models that inform fleet sizing, reservation versus on-demand mix, and pricing strategy for the MaaS product. Partner with infrastructure and finance teams to reconcile modeled costs against actual cloud and hardware spend, and maintain the analytical models that answer how many GPUs are needed and what they will cost with defensible numbers rather than gut calls.
  • Metric Definition Ownership: Define and maintain the canonical definitions for latency percentiles (time-to-first-token, inter-token latency, end-to-end), throughput, and utilization metrics used across engineering, product, and leadership dashboards, resolving disagreements between teams that compute the same-sounding metric differently. Document instrumentation requirements, aggregation windows, and edge-case handling so metric definitions stay stable as the platform and model catalog evolve, and audit dashboards for silent drift from the documented standard.
  • Cross-Team Performance Reporting: Build and maintain the dashboards, reports, and postmortem inputs that give engineering, product, and leadership a shared, trustworthy view of inference performance and cost trends, translating raw telemetry into decision-ready summaries. Act as the go-to reviewer whenever a performance or cost claim needs sanity-checking before it reaches a roadmap, pricing, or capacity decision, and coach other teams on correctly interpreting percentile and cost metrics.

How you will stand out:

  • Bring 5+ years of experience in performance engineering, capacity planning, or applied ML systems work on large-scale, GPU-backed or otherwise latency-sensitive distributed services, with at least part of that time spent directly on LLM or ML inference workloads.
  • Demonstrate hands-on experience characterizing production traffic statistically — building distributions of request rate, prompt and output token length, concurrency, and burstiness — using tools such as Python/pandas, SQL, Spark, or a comparable data-analysis stack.

  • Have experience designing, running, or auditing load-testing and benchmarking tooling (e.g., k6, Locust, custom load generators, or MLPerf-style suites) and reconciling their output against live production telemetry rather than treating benchmark numbers as ground truth.
  • Be comfortable partnering with finance/FinOps and infrastructure teams on GPU utilization and cost-per-token or cost-per-request modeling, including reasoning about on-demand, reserved, and spot capacity trade-offs.
  • Bring fluency with observability stacks such as Prometheus, Grafana, and distributed tracing tools, and a track record of defining metrics (latency percentiles, throughput, time-to-first-token) that hold up as the single source of truth across multiple teams.

Job Summary

The Risk Officer is a critical role within our cryptocurrency exchange in Bahrain. You will be responsible for developing, implementing, and monitoring the exchange's comprehensive risk management framework. This role requires a deep understanding of cryptocurrency markets, regulatory requirements, and risk management best practices to ensure our operations remain secure, compliant, and resilient.

Core Responsibilities

  • Framework Development: Design, implement, and maintain a comprehensive risk management framework addressing market, credit, operational, cybersecurity, AML/CFT, and regulatory risks.
  • Risk Assessment: Proactively identify and assess potential risks across trading, custody, compliance, technology, and operations using quantitative and qualitative methods.
  • Mitigation & Controls: Develop and implement risk mitigation strategies, policies, and controls relating to KYC/AML, transaction monitoring, cybersecurity, and data privacy.
  • Monitoring & Reporting: Track Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) against risk appetite and provide regular risk profile reports to senior management and the board.
  • Regulatory Compliance: Stay abreast of evolving local (Bahrain/CBB) and international cryptocurrency regulations, ensuring full framework alignment.
  • Cybersecurity & AML Collaboration: Partner closely with IT security to mitigate cyber threats (hacking, phishing) and collaborate with the compliance team on robust AML/CFT programs.
  • Incident Management: Design incident response plans, manage risk events, and conduct post-incident reviews to drive continuous improvement.
  • Culture & Training: Promote a strong internal risk culture by delivering training and awareness programs to employees across all departments.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Risk Management, Business Administration, or a related field. Master’s degree or professional certifications (FRM, APRM, PRM) preferred.
  • Experience: Minimum of 5–7 years in risk management, preferably within financial services. Experience in cryptocurrency or fintech sectors is highly desirable.
  • CBB Approved is desired for the role.
  • Domain Knowledge: Deep understanding of cryptocurrency markets, blockchain technology, associated risks, and relevant regulatory/AML frameworks.
  • Framework Expertise: Proven experience developing and implementing corporate risk methodologies and controls.
  • Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving skills, excellent cross-functional communication, independent work ethic, and high ethical standards.

Preferred Skills

  • Hands-on experience with specialized risk management software and tools.
  • Proficiency in data analytics and data visualization techniques.
  • Familiarity with global cybersecurity best practices.
  • Arabic language proficiency is a strong asset.
